Set Up A Projection Inside The Estimation Model

Source: R/setup_projection.R
Setup_Mod_Projection.Rd

Projects the population forward inside the model, so that sdreport gives standard errors for projected spawning biomass, catch, fishing mortality, numbers at age and stock status, with the uncertainty of the fit and of future recruitment in them. The projection is the same one Do_Population_Projection runs after a fit, but fed the model's own estimates rather than copies of them: the terminal year's numbers at age and F, the demographics averaged over the terminal years, and mean recruitment. Projection year 1 is the terminal assessment year run again, so year 2 is the first year after the assessment and the year catch advice is read from.

Usage

Setup_Mod_Projection(
  input_list,
  n_proj_yrs = 0,
  f_opt = "terminal",
  f_input = NULL,
  catch_input = NULL,
  f_ref_pt = NULL,
  b_ref_pt = NULL,
  hcr_function = hcr_threshold,
  hcr_scope = "region",
  F_constraint = NULL,
  refpt_type = "single_region",
  refpt_what = "SPR",
  SPR_x = NULL,
  sex_ratio_f = NULL,
  is_discard_fleet = NULL,
  local_bh_msy_newton_steps = 6,
  refpt_newton_steps = 2,
  refpt_log_f_start = log(0.1),
  n_avg_yrs = 1,
  sel_opt = "average",
  move_opt = "average",
  growth_opt = "average",
  rec_opt = "propagate",
  naa_opt = "propagate",
  calc_rec_st_yr = 1,
  rec_age = 1,
  calc_rec_yrs = NULL
)

Arguments

input_list

List with $data, $par and $map from the earlier setup calls.

n_proj_yrs

Integer. Number of years to project, counting the terminal assessment year, which is run again as projection year 1. 0 (default) leaves the projection off and the model as it was.

f_opt

How fishing mortality is set in the projection years. "terminal" (default) fishes every year at the terminal year's F. "input" fishes at the F given in f_input. "hcr" runs a harvest control rule on reference points given in f_ref_pt and b_ref_pt, treated as known numbers. "refpt" runs the rule on reference points the model solves for itself from its own estimates, so the uncertainty in F40, B40 or MSY is part of the projection's standard errors.

f_input

Array [n_regions, n_proj_yrs] of the F to fish at in each region and projection year, read under f_opt = "input". Year 1 replays the terminal year, so column 1 is not read.

catch_input

Retained catch to take in each region and projection year, an array [n_regions, n_proj_yrs], or [n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas] for catch by season, in the units of proj_Catch. The model finds the F that takes it, so the catch has no uncertainty and the uncertainty moves into that F and the projected biomass. A year left NA in every region is fished under f_opt, so known catch in the first years can be followed by the rule; a year is given in every region or in none. Year 1 replays the terminal year, so column 1 is not read. F_constraint applies only in the years left to f_opt. Default NULL, no catch given.

f_ref_pt

The F reference point the rule reads under f_opt = "hcr": the target F, one value per region, or [n_regions, n_proj_yrs] to vary it by year. A fixed number here, so its own uncertainty is not in the standard errors; f_opt = "refpt" is the way to include it.

b_ref_pt

The biomass reference point the rule reads under f_opt = "hcr": one value per population and region, or [n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs] to vary it by year. A fixed number here, as f_ref_pt is.

hcr_function

The harvest control rule: a function of x, the spawning biomass the rule reads, frp, the F reference point, and brp, the biomass reference point, returning the F to apply, as Do_Population_Projection takes it. Default hcr_threshold: the target F above brp, no fishing below 0.05 times brp, and a straight line between. For another cutoff, pass function(x, frp, brp) hcr_threshold(x, frp, brp, alpha = 0.1). A rule of your own runs inside the model, where the spawning biomass it is given is a quantity the model is differentiating, and such a quantity cannot be compared with > or <. Compare ad_value(x), the plain number, to decide which part of the rule applies, and use x itself in the arithmetic that follows, as hcr_threshold does.

hcr_scope

Which spawning biomass a region's rule reads. "region" (default), its own, against its own biomass reference point. "global", the total over regions against the reference points summed over regions, so every region shares one stock status.

F_constraint

A limit on the catch the rule's or input F would take. catch_cap lowers F wherever the catch would exceed a cap; catch_stability keeps the catch within a band of the previous year's, lowering or raising F; a list of them is applied in the order given, so put the cap last when nothing may exceed it. NULL (default) applies none.

refpt_type

Under f_opt = "refpt", "single_region" (default) or "multi_region", named as in Get_Reference_Points.

refpt_what

Under f_opt = "refpt", which reference point the model solves, named as in Get_Reference_Points: "SPR" (default) or "MSY" for one region, and "independent_SPR", "independent_MSY", "global_SPR", "global_MSY" or "local_MSY" for several. The MSY options need a model fitted with a stock-recruit curve.

SPR_x

The target spawning potential ratio for the SPR reference points, for example 0.4 for F40 and B40.

sex_ratio_f

Array [n_pop, n_regions]. Female share of recruits the per-recruit calculation behind the reference points starts from. Default NULL reads it from the model: in a two-sex model the recruitment sex ratio averaged over the last n_avg_yrs years, so an estimated sex ratio and its uncertainty reach the reference points; in a one-sex model 0.5, since the model halves its spawning biomass. A value given here is used instead, for instance to match a post hoc Get_Reference_Points run.

is_discard_fleet

Integer vector [n_fish_fleets], 1 for a fleet whose catch is discarded rather than landed, so the MSY options do not count it as yield. Default all zero.

local_bh_msy_newton_steps

Integer. Steps the local MSY solve takes for the equilibrium recruitment at each trial F. Default 6, as in Get_Reference_Points.

refpt_newton_steps

Integer. The reference points are solved numerically first, then refined with this many Newton steps that the model differentiates through, which is what gives a reference point its standard error. Default 2, which is enough. 0 leaves the reference points as fixed numbers with no standard error.

refpt_log_f_start

Numeric. Where the numerical solve for a reference point starts, on the log scale. Default log(0.1).

n_avg_yrs

Integer. How many terminal years weight at age, maturity, natural mortality, sex ratio and straying are averaged over, for the projection and for the reference points alike. Default 1, the terminal year alone.

sel_opt

Selectivity in the projection years. "average" (default) repeats its average over the last n_avg_yrs. "propagate" uses the years the model projected itself, which needs n_proj_yrs_devs in Setup_Mod_Dim and a time-varying selectivity, so its projected deviations and their uncertainty come along.

move_opt

Movement in the projection years, with the same two choices as sel_opt: "average" (default) over the last n_avg_yrs, or "propagate" from the years the model projected itself.

growth_opt

Weight at age in the projection years, when a growth model derives it (waa_model = "wt_len" in Setup_Mod_Biologicals). "average" (default) repeats its average over the last n_avg_yrs. "propagate" uses the years the model projected growth itself, which needs n_proj_yrs_devs in Setup_Mod_Dim, time-varying growth, and growth_tv_type = "curve", so the projected growth deviations and their uncertainty come along. Weight at age read from data has nothing to propagate and is always averaged.

rec_opt

Recruitment in the projection years, always mean recruitment over the years calc_rec_yrs picks, times a deviation. "propagate" (default) uses the deviations the model estimated for the projection years, which needs n_proj_yrs_devs in Setup_Mod_Dim. With no data behind them they sit at zero, so the projection runs at the mean, but each has the recruitment process error as its standard error, so the projected standard errors widen as a forecast's should. "mean" applies no deviation: recruitment is the mean, and its uncertainty is only that of the mean, which is small. "terminal" applies the terminal year's deviation in every projection year, one value shared by all of them, so the projected cohorts rise or fall together rather than averaging out.

naa_opt

The numbers at age state of a state-space model in the projection years. "propagate" (default) applies the state innovations the model estimated for the projection years, which needs n_proj_yrs_devs in Setup_Mod_Dim; they sit at their forecast, zero under "iid", and bring the state's process error into the standard errors. "terminal" advances the terminal year's state with no further innovations. Ignored by a model without a state.

calc_rec_st_yr

Integer. First model year of the window mean recruitment is averaged over, as in Get_Reference_Points; the window is calc_rec_st_yr:(n_years - rec_age). Default 1, the first model year.

rec_age

Integer. Years left off the end of that window, the most recent years whose recruitment is still poorly known. Default 1.

calc_rec_yrs

Integer vector of model years to average recruitment over instead of the window, for a mean that runs to the terminal year or skips years. Model year indices, 1 for the first year, not calendar years. Default NULL, the window.

Value

input_list with the settings stored in $data as proj_* fields.

Details

fit_model fits the model with the projection switched off, since the projection adds nothing to the likelihood, then rebuilds it at the estimates with the projection on.

See also

Other Reference Points and Projections: Do_Population_Projection(), Get_Reference_Point_Uncertainty(), Get_Reference_Points(), catch_cap(), catch_stability(), get_key_quants(), hcr_threshold()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# six years under the threshold rule on post hoc F40 and B40, capped at 25 kt
input_list <- Setup_Mod_Projection(input_list, n_proj_yrs = 6, f_opt = "hcr",
                                   f_ref_pt = refpts$f_ref_pt, b_ref_pt = refpts$b_ref_pt,
                                   F_constraint = catch_cap(25))
# 20 kt taken in each of the next two years, then the same rule
catch <- array(NA, dim = c(1, 6))
catch[1, 2:3] <- 20
input_list <- Setup_Mod_Projection(input_list, n_proj_yrs = 6, f_opt = "hcr",
                                   f_ref_pt = refpts$f_ref_pt, b_ref_pt = refpts$b_ref_pt,
                                   catch_input = catch)
fit <- fit_model(input_list$data, input_list$par, input_list$map, do_sdrep = TRUE)
fit$sd_rep # log_proj_SSB, log_proj_Catch, log_proj_F, log_proj_Total_Biom
} # }
